title: The Scientific Revolution
body:
# The Scientific Revolution

The Scientific Revolution (c. 1543-1687) marked a fundamental transformation in scientific thought, establishing the foundations of modern science.

## Key Developments

### Astronomy

**Copernicus (1473-1543)**
- Heliocentric model
- Earth revolves around Sun
- Published "On the Revolutions" (1543)
- Challenged 1,400 years of geocentrism

**Galileo (1564-1642)**
- Telescope observations
- Moons of Jupiter
- Phases of Venus
- Conflict with Church
- "Father of observational astronomy"

**Kepler (1571-1630)**
- Three laws of planetary motion
- Elliptical orbits
- Mathematical astronomy
- Harmony of the spheres

### Physics

**Newton (1643-1727)**
- Laws of motion
- Universal gravitation
- Calculus
- Optics
- Principia Mathematica (1687)
- "Standing on shoulders of giants"

### Medicine and Biology

**Vesalius (1514-1564)**
- Human anatomy
- Corrected Galen's errors
- Detailed illustrations

**Harvey (1578-1657)**
- Circulation of blood
- Heart as pump
- Experimental method

### Chemistry

**Boyle (1627-1691)**
- Boyle's Law (gases)
- Element concept
- Experimental chemistry
- "Father of modern chemistry"

## New Methods

### Empiricism
- Knowledge from observation
- Experiment over authority
- Francis Bacon's method
- Inductive reasoning

### Mathematics
- Nature written in mathematics (Galileo)
- Quantification
- Mathematical laws
- Predictive power

### Instruments
- Telescope
- Microscope
- Thermometer
- Barometer
- Air pump

## Institutional Changes

### Scientific Societies
- Royal Society (1660)
- French Academy (1666)
- Peer review
- Scientific journals

### Universities
- New subjects
- Experimental teaching
- Less theological focus

## Why It Mattered

### New Worldview
- Mechanical universe
- Natural laws
- Human reason can understand nature
- Progress possible

### Separation from Religion
- Nature as object of study
- Not animate or ensouled
- Gradual secularization
- Conflict with Church authority

### Foundation for Modern World
- Industrial Revolution
- Modern medicine
- Technology
- Scientific method established
